title: Sholazar Basin
body: Sholazar Basin is a hidden jungle in the northwest of Northrend, ringed by mountains, where the frozen continent gives way to steaming rivers, mangrove swamps and warm rain. Great crystal pillars rise around its edges, works of the titans, and the gorlocs who call themselves the Oracles tend ancient stone shrines they believe the Great Ones left for them. The wolvar of the Frenzyheart Tribe, newcomers to the basin, mean to take the land for their own, and the two peoples are at war. Rhinos, dreadsabers, primordial drakes and hydras roam the wilds, and they have drawn the famous hunter Hemet Nesingwary, whose expedition camps on a river in the west. The Venture Company digs at the foot of a pillar for its crystals. And in the east the Scourge has broken in: blight creeps over the Lost Lands, one of the pillars lies shattered, and a towering guardian, the Avatar of Freya, holds the line against the dead.

title: Wildgrowth Mangal
body: The Wildgrowth Mangal is a tangled mangrove swamp east of the Nesingwary Base Camp, its tall trees heavy with oranges, bananas and papayas that hang well out of reach. Emperor cobras and mangal crocolisks hunt among the roots, and the gorloc oracles prize the cobras' fangs. Not every visitor arrived by choice. The Venture Company has been shooting flying machines out of the sky over the swamp, and the wreck of one lies where it fell, its engine still whole. Nearby hangs Monte Muzzleshot, who parachuted into the mangal on his way to Hemet's camp with supplies, dangling from a tree by his tangled chute and waiting for someone to cut him down.

title: Nesingwary Base Camp
body: On a river in the west of the basin, Hemet Nesingwary's expedition has made its base camp after a hard landing: the ship that brought it ran aground, the brewer Grimbooze Thunderbrew lost his best kegs, and Weslex Quickwrench's flying machine, the Spirit of Gnomeregan, came through too damaged to fly, leaving the camp no way to send its reports home. Debaar, whom everyone seems to blame for the wreck, is tired of hearing about it. The hunters have not let it slow them. Hemet, Buck Cantwell, Debaar and Drostan test newcomers against the basin's beasts, Professor Calvert watches the strange weather, and Purser Boulian admits this is not what she signed up for, though at least it is warm.

parts.body: With an engine salvaged from a downed flying machine and spare parts carried off from the Venture Company's dig, Weslex has the Spirit of Gnomeregan flying again. She looks more like a Venture Company shredder now, and he warns riders not to complain about saw blades in their seats, but she carries travelers out of the camp. Her proper restoration will have to wait until the expedition is back in Dalaran.

title: The Bones of Nozronn
body: Across the river south of the Nesingwary Base Camp lie the Bones of Nozronn, the vast remains of a beast the gorlocs revere. Close by, in a small lean-to, lives Oracle Soo-rahm, who tends the bones and speaks for them. He asks no question of those who come to him, for he holds that mighty Nozronn already knows what is in their hearts. Still, the bones do not speak for nothing: a stranger must first bring offerings, such as the best fangs of the emperor cobras for the oracle's necklace, before Soo-rahm will light the incense.

parts.body: When the incense burned by Nozronn's head, a voice answered. It spoke of the shardhorn patriarch Farunn, who holds himself aloof from his brothers and walks alone north of the Bittertide Falls, needing no defenders. It ended with a warning: once Hemet had claimed his prize, he should leave this land in peace, for he does not belong here. Hemet would have none of it. No dead rhino, he said, tells Hemet Nesingwary where and what he can hunt.

title: Swindlegrin's Dig
body: Swindlegrin's Dig is a Venture Company mine on the far side of the Suntouched Pillar, northeast of the Nesingwary Base Camp. Goblin excavators and hired ruffians work it under Foreman Swindlegrin, who watches over the whole operation from a high platform with his ogre bodyguard, Meatpie, never far away. The goblins have decided the pillar and its crystals are theirs, and they do not welcome rivals: they shoot down the expedition's supply flights and their workers harass Hemet's scouts. They also hold a prisoner, an engineer of the expedition who came to study the crystals, and they hold her at the dig.

title: Lakeside Landing
body: River's Heart is the great lake near the center of the basin where its rivers converge, and on its northeastern shore lies Lakeside Landing. When the trouble with the Venture Company began, Hemet sent Marvin Wobblesprocket and his wife Tamara here with their flying machines, to set up a camp that could relay supplies into the basin and survey the land around it. Marvin gets so absorbed in his work that he hardly notices visitors. Tamara hopes to sharpen her own hunting skills between repairs, and Pilot Vic is ready to fly, if only he can find a copilot.

parts.body: Vic has flown over the northeast, and he is not sure what he saw there: to him it looked like a gigantic woman fighting the Scourge. The professor has spoken of a lifewarden appointed by the titans to watch over Sholazar, and Vic suspects this is her. He also knows that if the Scourge crosses from the Lost Lands into the rest of the basin, the expedition is as good as dead.

title: Frenzyheart Hill
body: Frenzyheart Hill is the home of the Frenzyheart Tribe, wolvar who came to Sholazar not long ago looking for a new home. High-Shaman Rakjak rules here, and he means for his people to take the basin for their own: the gorlocs, whom the wolvar call big-tongues, must leave or be killed. Elder Harkek is the gentler voice of the hill. The Frenzyheart can be vicious, he admits, but they are good people, friends with the smart and the strong; they just do not like the dumb. Trackers and berserkers guard the slopes, pups tumble between the huts, and young Rejek dreams aloud of the mighty warrior he will one day be.

title: Rainspeaker Canopy
body: Rainspeaker Canopy is a gorloc village in the boughs of an enormous tree, the home of the Rainspeaker tribe and the heart of the Oracles. Its people keep the Great Rain Stone, which they believe was left by the Great Ones who made them, and they care for it with offerings of shinies dug from the earth; in return, they say, it takes care of them. High-Oracle Soo-say leads them, and Oracle Soo-nee keeps songs of wind, water and crystal for friends with time to learn them. They call outsiders dryskins, and they call the wolvar puppy-men.

title: Mistwhisper Refuge
body: Mistwhisper Refuge lies near Bittertide Lake in the northwest of the basin, the home of the Mistwhisper gorlocs and their Great Mist Stone. The stone is one of the Oracles' weather shrines, fed with crystals, and the Mistwhispers use it to call up mists that hide the land all around. They know just which crystals to use; set the wrong ones before the stone and its clouds, rain and lightning run wild. Their neighbors are no comfort. North of the village, at the Spearborn Encampment, Frenzyheart spearbearers and scavengers have pitched a camp of their own.

title: Kartak's Hold and Sparktouched Haven
body: In the far southwest of the basin the war between the wolvar and the gorlocs burns hottest. Kartak's Hold is a Frenzyheart stronghold, crowded with ravagers and hunters, and close beside it lies Sparktouched Haven, where the Sparktouched gorlocs guard their Great Lightning Stone. The two camps are hardly apart at all. Sparktouched warriors and oracles fight the wolvar among the huts of both, and neither side gives ground for long.

parts.body: To the friends of the Frenzyheart, the hold shows more. Shaman Jakjek stands among the wolvar there in the thick of the battle, and he sees to it that Kartak, for whom the hold is named, never goes hungry. Kartak comes for big-tongue meat, he says, and the Frenzyheart make sure plenty is ready, so that Kartak does not eat them instead.

parts.body: Kartak is a great beast, and blood is how the wolvar call it. Oracle blood laid on the altar in the hold brings Kartak to a feast of big-tongues, and if a hunter is worthy, Kartak takes that hunter's body and lends its rage to the slaughter of the Sparktouched.

Lightningcaller Soo-met keeps the Great Lightning Stone here, and though the puppy-men have attacked for days, he says the stone is still safe. Soo-holu has come to help the Sparktouched many times before, and the wolvar, he is sure, do not stand a chance.

It does not know anything is wrong until the shrines are disturbed, so a tainted crystal taken from the wolvar and brought to the Great Lightning Stone calls it to help. Those it trusts, it lets share its body, and through them it turns its power on the Frenzyheart.

title: Dorian's Outpost
body: Dorian's Outpost is the expedition's northern camp, pitched across Bittertide Lake by Dorian Drakestalker, who came looking for bigger game than rhinos and cats. He found it. Primordial drakes rule the Savage Thicket to the north and east, beasts that can devour a man whole, and their queen, Broodmother Slivina, nests on a perch at its northern edge. Farther on lie the Bonefields, where goretalon rocs feed on the corpses of old mammoths. In camp, Zootfizzle raises the hatchlings Dorian brings in and declares the outpost a cog-free zone, and Colvin Norrington gathers talons and other reagents for Archmage Pentarus of Dalaran, who helped fund the expedition.

parts.body: Broodmother Slivina is dead. Hemet Nesingwary himself rode against her on the back of a shattertusk mammoth named Stampy, and when it was over he told Dorian the tale: the shaking ride, the fearsome beast, the haze of blood, lead and sweat as her attacks came faster and faster. Dorian, who spent the fight tending the fire and arguing about cogs with Zootfizzle, insists that was epic too, in its own way.

title: The Crystal Pillars
body: Great pillars of crystal rise around the edges of Sholazar Basin, and four of them still stand: the Glimmering, the Suntouched, the Mosslight and the Skyreach. They are works of the titans, and the gorlocs, who call their makers the Great Ones, hold them sacred and teach songs to be played at their summits. Blue crystal formations from the Skyreach gather along the southern river, and the Venture Company digs in the shadow of the Suntouched. At the Glimmering Pillar, the servants of Freya stand watch, and they are not alone there: cultists have been seen skulking at its foot.

parts.body: The Avatar of Freya tells what the pillars are for. There were five, set around the basin by the titans, who shaped whole forms of life here and let them grow unchecked, and the pillars pour out pure lifeforce. While all five stood, the Scourge could never have broken into the basin. But one of them, the Lifeblood Pillar, has been destroyed.

title: The Lifeblood Pillar
body: The Lifeblood Pillar, once one of the great crystal pillars of the basin, lies broken. It came down with such force that the earth heaved, and its largest piece, the Sundered Shard, rests where it fell, a cave gaping in its side. Lifeblood elementals drift among the scattered red crystal, and shards of the pillar's power glitter in the soil. The Scourge walks here now: bonescythe ravagers and monstrous wights stalk the wreckage, and corpses are being dragged toward the Shard.

parts.body: No undead could have come near the pillar while it stood, so whoever brought it down was alive. At its foot lay a badly burnt corpse among the remains of powder kegs: one of the Cult of the Damned, the Lich King's living servants, sent where the dead could not go. The pillar fell to their explosives, and through the breach it left, the Scourge came in.

title: Mosswalker Village
body: Mosswalker Village sits up the ridge northeast of the broken Lifeblood Pillar, the home of the Mosswalker gorlocs and their Great Moss Stone. It is a village of the dead now. Its people lie slaughtered or dying in the moss, blighted corpses and bonescythe ravagers prowl between the huts, and the bodies of the fallen are being dragged away. At Rainspeaker Canopy, Soo-say knew only that the Mosswalkers had stopped coming to the shrine.

parts.body: Not every Mosswalker was lost. Moodle of the Rainspeakers went through the village with a companion, cutting down the dead and searching the fallen, and some of the gorlocs were still alive. The survivors were sent on to Rainspeaker Canopy. Moodle, who talks down to his people at every turn, admitted he never wants to see any of them die; the Mosswalkers, he said, were good people, and they did not deserve this.

title: The Blight Line
body: Beyond the Rainspeaker Rapids, the green of Sholazar ends at the Blight Line. Beyond it lie the Lost Lands, sick and grey, where blighted corpses and bonescythe ravagers roam and the Scourge's blight spreaders poison the ground, and among them stalks Thalgran Blightbringer. Along the line, the servants of Freya stand against the dead, and at the Rainspeaker Rapids walks the Avatar of Freya herself, a towering guardian who swears to crush every last one of the Scourge's decrepit bones under her heel.

parts.body: Thalgran Blightbringer was the monster most to blame for corrupting the land, the Avatar said, and she sent an ally against him with her ward. It caught his death bolts and turned them back upon him sevenfold until he fell. In these lands, where the power of life rules, she warned, all harm the Lich King's agents inflict will be returned to them sevenfold.

title: The Avalanche
body: In the east of the basin the jungle vanishes under a great slide of snow and ice called the Avalanche, and here the Scourge has the run of the land. Snowblind ghouls and frostbitten corpses crowd it in their hundreds, frosthowl screechers circle above, and risen reavers lumber among them. Mighty servants of the Lich King drive the host on: Urgreth of the Thousand Tombs, who swears this land is the Lich King's now, Bythius the Flesh-Shaper and Hailscorn, with Glonn and Cerberon beside them.

parts.body: Here the Avatar of Freya unleashed the Etymidian. The colossus strode into the Avalanche and tore through the Scourge host, two hundred of its minions and more, and Bythius the Flesh-Shaper, Urgreth of the Thousand Tombs and Hailscorn fell beneath it. The Avatar gave her thanks: life in the basin would go on thriving, while the forces of death raged in the lands around it.

title: The Makers' Perch and the Waygate
body: Three works of the titans keep their silence at the edges of the basin. The Makers' Perch stands on the western rim and the Makers' Overlook high in the eastern mountains, halls of titan stone where stone guardians still stand watch; in the overlook rests a timeworn coffer, locked fast, whose huge stone key one of the guardians carries. At the southern end of the basin stands the third, a titan waygate.

title: The Stormwright's Shelf
body: The Stormwright's Shelf is a broad, flat ledge outside the basin's lip in the far northwest, above the Makers' Perch, and few reach it without wings. Storms rule it. Storm revenants and aqueous spirits, the sons of wind and water, roam the rock, giant stormwatchers of metal stand among them, and on the shelf's western side lies the gorlocs' Shrine of the Tempest. Low mounds of soaked, fertile earth dot the ground, each holding a strong seed that waits, the gorlocs say, only for the right song.

parts.body: The Oracles hear an ancient song in the storms of the shelf, the Song of Wind and Water. Played on tempest drums, it calls Haiphoon, the Great Tempest, who devours the sons of typhoon and storm so that the tempest may continue, and the gorlocs believe the Great Tempest looks with favor on those who help him feed.

title: Avatar of Freya
body: The Avatar of Freya is a towering guardian who walks the Rainspeaker Rapids, where the green of the basin meets the blight. The expedition's professor speaks of a lifewarden appointed by the titans to look over Sholazar, and she fits the description. The Scourge are a blemish on her pristine lands, and she has sworn by the might of her creators to crush every last one of them. She has no patience for strangers: she knows outlanders are not of this land, and any who will not fight the Lich King's minions are told to leave before they distract her from her duties.

parts.body: Once trust is earned she names herself plainly: the embodiment of a single aspect of Freya, daughter of the titans, left here as the Lifewarden to protect the land against the Scourge. She never imagined the Lich King would send willing living servants to do his work. She could crush them herself, but she cannot leave her post, for she is all that stands between the undead armies and the rest of the basin.

title: High-Shaman Rakjak
body: High-Shaman Rakjak leads the Frenzyheart Tribe from Frenzyheart Hill, and he wants one thing: the land for the Frenzyheart, with the big-tongues gone or dead. He laughs easily, mostly at others, and he is always short of slaves. Outsiders who cross his hunters, such as any stranger who steals a kill from Tracker Gekgek, find themselves sent to him as the tribe's newest slave and put to work hunting the basin's apes and wasps beside Frenzyheart hunters who are in no hurry to let them forget it.

parts.body: A slave who hunts well can win him over. Rakjak laughed long at the tale of the lightning at Mistwhisper Refuge, and he told the slave who had helped call it down that one day, maybe, such a hunter could be an honorary Frenzyheart. Then he gave his most important task: find the injured big-tongue a tracker had spotted by the river and bring it back alive, not to kill it, but to hide it away and poke it until it told him things.

title: Zepik the Gorloc Hunter
body: Zepik is the best hunter of the Frenzyheart, and his favorite prey is the gorlocs. Apes and wasps bore him; the big-tongues, he says, are not as dumb as the other hunts and give a real fight. He learned to hunt his own way rather than Dajik's, and not long ago he traveled much of the world on his own; he loves stories of beasts, dragons and gods. Now he sets out on long treks to break the gorloc shrines and frighten their people from the land, and he is glad of a partner who can keep up.

parts.body: The lich Artruis seized Zepik and used him as a pawn, and only the one who chose to stand with him set him free. Zepik called his rescuer a friend he knew better than any wolvar did, no traitor whatever the others said, and offered to convince the tribe that his rescuer had saved him and beaten the big-tongues. Yet even Zepik, no friend of big-tongues, felt a little bad for the gorloc who died that way: those who fight that well, he said, deserve a fair fight.

title: High-Oracle Soo-say
body: High-Oracle Soo-say leads the Oracles from Rainspeaker Canopy, where he keeps the Great Rain Stone and brings it the shinies his people dig up. He is kindly and quick to welcome any stranger who helps his people, though he has a habit of staring at a visitor's forehead while he talks. His Rainspeakers were in the basin long before the wolvar came, and their home is a sacred place; whatever the puppy-men do, Soo-say will not leave it.

parts.body: What Soo-say wants is peace. He once sent the Frenzyheart shaman Vekjik an offering and a promise that the Oracles would play nice, and Vekjik answered only with threats. Soo-say was left hurt and puzzled. His people only try to be nice, he says, and the puppy-men only ever answer by being mean; they keep meddling with the great stones, as if they do not know the stones are sacred.

title: Moodle
body: Moodle is no ordinary Rainspeaker. He has been out in the world and learned the language of outsiders, and he wants it understood at once that he is not as foolish as most Oracles a stranger meets, nor easily duped. Sharp of tongue and weary of running errands for people he has only just met, he has little faith in Soo-say's forgiving ways: as Moodle sees it, the wolvar will never leave the gorlocs alone, and the only way to stop them is to kill them. There is no peace.

parts.body: Moodle saw what others missed. The undead were never supposed to be able to enter the basin, and he judged that the fall of the Lifeblood Pillar must have let them in; he only wished he had understood sooner how much the pillars and the great stones mattered. Following the corpses the dead were dragging away, he came to suspect that their leader lay inside the Sundered Shard, and sent his companion in after it while he carried the news to Soo-say.

title: Jaloot
body: Jaloot is a Rainspeaker gorloc bursting with energy, who digs faster than anyone, can never have too many shiny crystals, and treasures one favorite crystal above all the rest. Soo-say sends him out with friendly dryskins as a companion, and a cheerful one he is: he chatters about the Great Ones, who he thinks keep the Oracles safe because they know the gorlocs are good and nice, boasts at every fallen foe, and wants nothing more than for his new friends to stay his friends.

parts.body: The lich Artruis took Jaloot captive and used him as a pawn in the Sundered Shard. When the one who chose the Oracles' side set him free, he was overjoyed. He had seen his friend strike down the puppy-man who had been held there with him, and he was sure it meant that the dryskin was done with the wolvar for good and a friend now of all Oracles.

title: Artruis the Heartless
body: Artruis the Heartless, Moodle believes, is the leader of the undead who have poured into Sholazar since the Lifeblood Pillar fell. The trail of corpses his servants drag away points to his lair inside the Sundered Shard, the great fallen piece of the pillar. Moodle wants him found and slain, so that no one is left to drive the dead back upon the gorlocs, but he cannot go himself; whoever goes must find other help.

parts.body: Artruis, a lich, was waiting. Two brave, ignorant fools, he said, a wolvar and a gorloc who despised each other, had both spoken of their hero, so he had bound them both and shielded himself, offering the hero a chance to choose a side: his spell would hold until the choice was made. He boasted of a hundred years of war and claimed that he could not die, but the shattered crystals of the pillar weakened him, and he fell. Inside his phylactery lay an endless void, and far off, something screaming.

title: The Stranded Expedition
body: When Archmage Pentarus of Dalaran heard that the legendary Hemet Nesingwary was setting sail for Sholazar Basin, a land said to be a lush paradise in the middle of a frozen continent, he offered to help fund the expedition in return for samples of its exotic plants, reagents and crystals. Then the reports stopped coming. The expedition's ship had run aground, and its flying machine came through too badly damaged to carry word home. Worse, the Venture Company, digging at the Suntouched Pillar, was harassing Hemet's scouts and shooting down his supply flights, and Monte Muzzleshot, sent with supplies, ended up hanging by his parachute from a tree in the swamp.

parts.body: Debaar would not let the insult stand: Hemet's expedition came to hunt, and hunt it would. The company's workers at Swindlegrin's Dig were cut down, and Foreman Swindlegrin and his ogre bodyguard Meatpie with them. Debaar was relieved to be rid of the trouble, though it was not a fight she would have joined herself. A game hunter, she says, cannot in good conscience lift her weapon against another person.

parts.body: One of the expedition was still missing. Engineer Helice had gone to the Suntouched Pillar to explore its crystals and take samples, and the goblins had overpowered her and kept her at the dig. Freed at last, she fought her way out, blowing up the company's own cartloads of explosives as she went, and made it back to camp, where everyone had begun to worry when she did not return.

title: The Great Hunt
body: No rough landing will stop Hemet Nesingwary from mastering the largest game Sholazar has to offer, and his companions test every newcomer who wants a place in the hunt. Hemet sends them first against the mighty shardhorn rhinos in the wilds northwest of camp. Buck Cantwell, kept in camp by his injuries, sets them on the dreadsabers, cats that bring down larger game than any he has seen a cat hunt. Debaar, who wants no jokes about the shipwreck, pits them against the mangal crocolisks, wily masters of the ambush. Each of these trials ends, in time, with a single legendary beast.

parts.body: The rhino patriarch Farunn, found with the help of a gorloc oracle and the bones of a dead rhino, fell near the shore of Bittertide Lake, and Hemet, turning its horn in his hands, called it an astounding trophy. Then his eyes turned north. There were rumors, he said, of even bigger, more ferocious game in the northern reaches of the basin.
sources: quest 12556 description and reward text (Farunn on the northeast shore of Bittertide Lake; an astounding trophy; even bigger game in the northern reaches)

parts.body: Buck had heard the natives tell of a great dreadsaber they call Shango, but his injuries kept him from looking for proof. Tracks found on the southern shore of Bittertide Lake proved the tale, and Shango was stalked to the falls that feed the lake and slain there. His pelt, Buck declared, was exquisite, and the pursuit flawless: the work of a true huntsman.

parts.body: Debaar's plan for the crocolisk they call Bushwhacker was to beat the ambusher at his own game, hiding a hunter on the western beach of River's Heart under a disguise of sandfern. The disguise did not fool him. The kill happened all the same, and Debaar, a little put out, had to admit that the jaw was truly a monster's and that Hemet would be proud.

title: Frenzyheart and the Oracles
body: The wolvar of the Frenzyheart and the gorlocs of the Oracles are at war over Sholazar, and outsiders are drawn in whether they like it or not. Stealing a kill from the wolvar tracker Gekgek is enough to make a stranger the tribe's newest slave, sent to Frenzyheart Hill and set to hunting hardknuckle apes and sapphire wasps under hunters like the boastful Goregek and the forgetful Dajik. Hunt well enough and the tribe may come to respect its slave, and the Frenzyheart have no shortage of enemies to hunt.

parts.body: Rakjak sent his best slave with Zepik on a long trek to Mistwhisper Refuge. Zepik knew the gorlocs fed their rain shrines with crystals and that the wrong ones drove the clouds mad, so the two smashed blue crystals before the Great Mist Stone. Lightning struck an oracle down, Zepik cackled with glee, and the hunters killed Mistwhispers until it was time to walk home. Back on the hill, Rakjak laughed too.

parts.body: Rakjak wanted a wounded gorloc brought in alive, to hide and question. But the injured Rainspeaker, terrified and grateful to be spared, asked its captor to come home with it instead, since the puppy-men were kind of mean anyway. At Rainspeaker Canopy the Oracles eyed the stranger who stank of puppy-men, then welcomed the one who had helped them.

Mistcaller Soo-gan, who thought the newcomer's face somehow familiar, trusted Soo-say's word and asked for help. Tartek was slain, the treasure taken back, and the spearbearers at the wolvar camp to the north cut down. The Mistcaller was sure the puppy-men would leave them alone now.

title: The Lifewarden's War
body: The forces of undeath have broken into Sholazar, the very cradle of life, and along the Blight Line the Avatar of Freya fights them almost alone. She trusts no outsider. Any stranger who means to stay must first prove they are no minion of the Lich King by destroying the blighted corpses and bonescythe ravagers of the Lost Lands. Even then she is slow to judge, but she allows that there may be something such a stranger can do for her, for the titans' creations must be defended.

parts.body: The trail of the pillar's destroyer changed everything. The Avatar had been searching for the wrong enemy all along, for she had never imagined that the living would willingly serve the Lich King. Learning that the Cult of the Damned was at work in her lands, she wasted no time: the cultists, she declared, would be uprooted from Sholazar.
sources: quest 12608 reward text (the living willingly serve the Lich King? all this time I've been searching for the wrong enemy; uproot these cultists from these lands)

parts.body: The cultists had made their camp at the Death's Hand Encampment, with explosives they meant to turn on the land, and they were cut down there. It came too late. Even as the camp fell, the Avatar sensed more of them at the Glimmering Pillar, making ready to bring it down as they had the Lifeblood, and she gave her ally a horn to blow atop the pillar and channel her power through its crystal.
sources: quests 12617 and 12660 descriptions and reward text (Death's Hand Encampment; cultist infiltrators; unstable explosives; dealt with, but it might have been too late)
quest 12620 description (cultists at the Glimmering Pillar preparing to destroy it; blow this horn atop the pillar to channel my power through the crystal)

parts.body: The Avatar's power broke the cultists at the Glimmering Pillar, and she owned that a mere mortal had proved a worthier ally than she expected. It was not enough. The Scourge showed no sign of stopping and was gathering for a final push, and the Avatar spoke of a last resort, one she would reveal only to someone whose trust was absolute, and from which there would be no turning back.

title: The Avatar's Last Resort
body: As the Scourge gathers for a final push, the Avatar of Freya turns to a last resort, one she will reveal only to an ally whose trust in her is absolute. Its first step is to wake a waygate of the titans. The switches that power it lie in the old vantage points from which the titans watched over their creations, and the first waits inside the Makers' Perch on the western edge of the basin, where many of their stone servants still stand guard. It is only the first of two.

parts.body: The second switch lay in the Makers' Overlook, high in the eastern mountains. With both thrown, the waygate at the southern end of the basin woke for the first time in seven centuries. Through it, the Avatar said, lay the basin's final hope, the weapon called the Etymidian, and with it she meant to put an end to those who would bring the taint of undeath to her pristine land.
sources: quest 12613 description and reward text (a second vantage point to the east, high in the mountains; the waygate is active)
quest 12548 description and log text (the Waygate in the southern end of Sholazar Basin, activated for the first time in seven centuries; where our final hope lies; unleash the Etymidian)

parts.body: Beyond the gate, in a distant land, stood a colossus of stone. The engravings carved upon it left no doubt that this was the weapon the Avatar had spoken of. This was the Etymidian.
sources: quest 12548 reward text (as you read the engravings on this stone colossus, you realize this is the weapon Freya spoke of)

parts.body: Once awake, the Etymidian sensed the essence of Sholazar fraying under the blight of undeath. Only Freya's power could grant it passage into her lands, so it bound its being into a rune, to be carried back through the waygate to the Avatar. When the rune reached her hands, she spoke a promise: woe to all who serve the Lich King and threaten the titans' creations, for the Etymidian is here.
